name: Pūjyapāda Devanandin
dates_notes: Usually placed in the sixth century, but the dates derive from literary and traditional evidence rather than a contemporary dated record.
core_thesis: Pūjyapāda's *Sarvārthasiddhi* is the earliest extant Digambara commentary on Umāsvāti's *Tattvārthasūtra*. It makes the compact doctrinal framework of the root text usable as a systematic account of knowledge, substances, karma, ethical discipline, and liberation, and became a foundational source for later Digambara scholasticism.

engaged_works.title: Sarvarthasiddhi
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Uniformly ascribed to Pūjyapāda in the Digambara commentary tradition; the Sanskrit text survives in editions and translations.
engaged_works.summary: A Sanskrit commentary on all ten chapters of the *Tattvārthasūtra*. It gives a sustained Digambara exposition of its categories and supplies an essential bridge between Umāsvāti's aphoristic text and the later dialectical commentaries of Akalaṅka and Vidyānanda.
